certificate.family: NEAR core staking pool v0.4.0 (near/core-contracts@1cacc9d), the code of *.poolv1.near pools
certificate.statement: In the Lean model: from any state reachable from new() without outflow from the pool account, a delegator with stake can call unstake_all, which succeeds and leaves it at least get_account_total_balance; then, with no further calls by it, in any state 4 or more epochs later in which the protocol has returned the unstaked stake, withdraw_all succeeds and sends it at least that amount. No call by another account, the pool owner included, lowers its unstaked balance, unlock epoch or shares; the share price never decreases.
assumptions: The theorem is about a model; the deployed bytes are tied to it by hash equality with the committed artifact and by execution on the nearcore runtime (tested, not proved).
The protocol has returned the unstaked stake by the time of withdraw_all (an assumption about NEAR, checked on simulator runs).
No outflow from the pool account other than withdraw (no access keys; no slashing in NEAR today).
Storage staking is not modelled: if the storage cost exceeded the pool's remaining balance, the last withdrawal would wait for a top-up.
Fewer than 10^12 calls to the pool in its lifetime; enough gas attached; staking-key validity rules unchanged.
certificate.binding: deployed code hash equals staking-pool/res/staking_pool.wasm committed at near/core-contracts@1cacc9d; pool accounts created by poolv1.near have no access keys

conformance.runtime: nearcore 2.14.0 (protocol 88) via near-contract-sim; state compared after every step; 20998/20998 error texts equal
